title: Black Cat
summary: Black Cat is the user-facing brand for the Portable Trusted Linux (PTL) project. The M13B no-typing System Check was physically exercised on real hardware and its duplicate-execution report-permission defect is fixed in source. The previously frozen candidate remains superseded pending a corrected integrated rebuild and physical retest. The first large text-encoded boot splash failed CI decoding before image construction; it has been removed and replaced by a deliberately smaller 160x120, 8-colour Black Cat splash whose decoded bytes are SHA-256 pinned and validated before staging. The Black Cat Automation Manifesto remains mandatory: safe, reversible, auditable work proceeds automatically until a genuine human gate is reached. The separate Approved Black Cat ISO release gate remains closed.

candidate.note: SUPERSEDED TEST CANDIDATE — DO NOT USE FOR M13B COMPLETION. Physical testing confirmed the no-typing System Check boots and displays observations, but exposed duplicate execution: the root systemd service created /run/blackcat reports and the normal-user profile hook attempted to run the collector again, causing Permission denied on report writes. Source is fixed so systemd is the sole producer and the login hook only displays the existing report. A corrected integrated rebuild — now also carrying compact reproducible Black Cat boot branding — must pass before a new Current Test Candidate is published.

release.note: No Black Cat ISO is currently an approved release. Development candidates remain separate from release approval. After physical and later release gates are met, one exact ISO may be deliberately promoted and this record will publish its approved identity.

sections.title: Automation Manifesto — proceed by default
sections.content: Black Cat engineering follows a mandatory autonomy policy: proceed automatically through safe, reversible, auditable, already-authorized work. Before asking the operator to proceed, confirm a routine next step, or pausing merely because CI is running, the assistant must run the pre-pause check. It must first ask whether an authorized tool can perform the next step, whether the action is reversible/non-destructive, whether missing information can be retrieved from GitHub/CI/artifacts/logs/the builder, whether independent safe work remains, and whether a clear bounded defect can be fixed and regression-tested automatically. If those tests permit continuation, do not pause for routine permission. Genuine human gates are physical hardware interaction, destructive or difficult-to-reverse actions, platform/trust-ownership changes, new credentials or authorization, secret exposure risk, financial/legal/public-release commitments, material security-policy choices, or essential information that genuinely cannot be derived safely. When a pause is required, state exactly which human gate was reached and why automation cannot safely cross it. Full policy: docs/11-automation-manifesto.md.

sections.title: Black Cat visual identity and boot branding
sections.content: The supplied Black Cat project icon is the visual source for future system imagery and icons. The first 320x240 text-encoded splash failed CI before image construction because its repository base64 was invalid. That malformed asset was removed. The current source is a deliberately smaller 160x120, 8-colour PNG carried as 4,188 bytes of base64 text at assets/blackcat-boot-160x120.png.b64. The decoded splash SHA-256 is 24d03a442c3f7f04a060d30fbf8710f8b8cd2b5495caffdeea7cc47fcbc546ea. Build preparation validates source existence, successful base64 decode and exact SHA-256 before staging the same bytes into the GRUB/UEFI and Syslinux/legacy bootloader trees. Static checks independently repeat decode/digest validation and require both menu configurations to reference the splash. Branding remains cosmetic: inability to render the image must not determine trust, evidence classification or whether ordinary boot choices remain usable.

sections.title: Branding boundary
sections.content: Black Cat is the user-facing project/product name. Portable Trusted Linux remains the technical description and PTL remains the stable internal engineering shorthand in repository paths, PTL_ variables, workflows and existing evidence identifiers.

sections.title: Current focus
sections.content: All active engineering is focused on Black Cat / Portable Trusted Linux Prototype 1. Community Compute Commons remains paused.

sections.title: Core trust chain
sections.content: Authenticated release reference -> verified USB image -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot and TCG event log -> TPM PCR evidence -> signed UKI -> authenticated dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed disposable state -> nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Development candidate versus approved release
sections.content: The living project page may expose exactly one Current Test Candidate only when its exact identity is explicit and its automated smoke test has passed. A physical-test defect supersedes that candidate and disables its development download until a corrected rebuild passes the gates. The separate Approved Black Cat ISO record remains disabled until explicit release promotion requirements are met.

sections.title: Fail-closed project viewer
sections.content: The cPanel-hosted public viewer accepts the GitHub read-only credential only from /home/learning/.blackcat/github_token, outside the public web root. The enclosing directory and token file must have no group/world permission bits. There is no environment-variable, hard-coded-token or offline authoritative-cache fallback. Missing, unsafe or invalid credential/data state causes a fail-closed response and no approved ISO download.

sections.title: Current automated rebuild evidence
sections.content: Black Cat Boot Smoke Test run 34684121916 failed during build preparation before Debian image construction. GNU base64 reported invalid input while reconstructing the first large 320x240 branding asset, so no conclusion about Debian, GRUB, Syslinux, the System Check or QEMU bootability follows from that run. The malformed asset has been removed and replaced by the compact independently hash-pinned 160x120 source. A replacement CI run on the repaired branch head is the next automated evidence gate.

sections.title: CI concurrency discipline
sections.content: PR workflow path filters are evaluated against the pull request's changed-file set, so later metadata commits can still retrigger build workflows when the PR already contains build changes. Per-PR concurrency collapses obsolete work. Hosted/read-only jobs may cancel superseded in-progress copies; the self-hosted live-build preserves an active chroot build and only collapses pending duplicates.

sections.title: Physical System Check result
sections.content: The frozen M13B candidate physically reached the no-typing Black Cat System Check and displayed observations without operator command entry. The photographed screen reported UEFI, Secure Boot ENABLED, TPM DEVICE_FOUND, TCG EVENT LOG FOUND, DM-VERITY ROOT NOT_ACTIVE, NETWORK LINK NO_ACTIVE_LINK_OBSERVED, kernel 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 and x86_64. These remain OBSERVED results, not universal trust claims.

sections.title: Duplicate diagnostic execution fix
sections.content: Physical testing exposed Permission denied when writing /run/blackcat/quick-check.txt and quick-check.json. Source review showed blackcat-check.service had already run as root and created the reports, then the normal-user profile hook executed the collector a second time. The service is now the sole evidence producer; the profile hook waits for and displays its report only. Static checks reject any future direct collector invocation from the profile hook.

sections.title: Evidence classification
sections.content: The quick-check screen reports observations and does not become its own ultimate verifier. Individual observations remain OBSERVED/UNKNOWN/etc. until stronger cryptographic and independent verification gates are implemented.

sections.title: Verified builder toolchain
sections.content: The remote Debian 13 builder has the declared live-build, xorriso, verity, UKI, signing and TPM tooling installed. It remains a builder rather than an attestation target because the cloud VM does not expose the required UEFI/TPM interfaces.

sections.title: Build provenance
sections.content: The prior physical-test ISO recorded source commit c65c1cf27fc8bf21bbbb95d5bca989bed54e34df, run 34669451222, size 376438784 bytes and SHA-256 34903e52268bf995207cc51e86de9d1950406690445fca7cedfe5a98371f7b32. That identity remains preserved as evidence but the candidate is superseded for M13B completion.

sections.title: Immediate evidence gate
sections.content: M13 is complete and M13B remains current. Physical testing proved the no-typing path reaches the diagnostic screen, while exposing a report-saving bug that is fixed in source. The branch also carries compact reproducible Black Cat boot branding. Automation continues through replacement static checks, live-build and integrated UEFI/QEMU smoke gates without routine operator permission. The next genuine human gate is reached only after one exact new candidate passes those gates and requires physical USB writing/boot testing.

sections.title: Progressive hardening
sections.content: Prototype stages may temporarily use weaker controls to prove the workflow, but every such control must document its trust assumption, compromise path, temporary justification and stronger replacement. Bootstrap credentials, the self-hosted runner, the cPanel read-only repository token, GitHub Actions artifact distribution and temporary live-build privilege are not final security controls; signing keys must never be placed in the viewer credential path.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons discipline
sections.content: Every meaningful session updates docs/07-lessons-learned.md and affected specifications or decisions. project_content.json is always written last.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security components
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKI, TPM 2.0 and dm-verity rather than inventing replacement primitives.

decisions.title: Independent verification is mandatory
decisions.text: The target computer cannot be the sole authority deciding that its own measurements are trustworthy.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Documents, source and the living JSON index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory output
decisions.text: Every meaningful engineering/research session records lessons before project_content.json is updated last.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 baseline is Debian 13/trixie amd64
decisions.text: Exact build-host and package versions are captured as provenance.

decisions.title: Community Compute Commons paused
decisions.text: The research remains preserved, but active implementation returns exclusively to the core trust chain until its initial acceptance gates pass.

decisions.title: Progressive hardening is mandatory
decisions.text: Temporary weaker controls may be used to make demonstrable progress only when their assumptions, weaknesses and stronger replacements are explicit. They must never be presented as final security controls.

decisions.title: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner is the initial remote execution path
decisions.text: Repository-scoped Actions jobs provide the auditable control path into the disposable build VM. Privileged operations remain explicitly separated from the unprivileged runner.

decisions.title: Build host and attestation target are separate roles
decisions.text: The DigitalOcean VM is used for building and artifact generation. UEFI measured-boot and TPM attestation claims require a separate platform that exposes those interfaces.

decisions.title: Normalize builder capability checks
decisions.text: Host preflight uses a deterministic system PATH so service-account environment differences cannot silently hide installed administrative tools.

decisions.title: Privilege only the live-build construction stage
decisions.text: Live-build preparation is unprivileged. The actual lb build operation is the current explicit privileged boundary and any passwordless permission used for Prototype 1 is temporary, documented and subject to later hardening.

decisions.title: Record source identity separately from checkout identity
decisions.text: CI manifests record intended source commit/ref separately from the temporary merge/detached checkout identity that a pull-request workflow may use.

decisions.title: Black Cat is the user-facing brand
decisions.text: Keep PTL internal engineering identifiers stable while presenting the product/project to users as Black Cat.

decisions.title: No-typing hardware diagnostics
decisions.text: Provide a dedicated Black Cat System Check boot menu entry that automatically collects modular runtime observations and presents a photograph-friendly screen.

decisions.title: Physical boot is an observation, not attestation
decisions.text: A successful USB boot proves bootability on the tested configuration only and must not be promoted to Secure Boot, TPM, dm-verity, firmware or release-authenticity assurance.

decisions.title: Approved releases are separate from CI candidates
decisions.text: The public project viewer only exposes an approved ISO after one exact candidate is deliberately promoted and its filename, byte size, SHA-256, source identity and test state are recorded. This reduces operator error but does not replace future cryptographic release signing.

decisions.title: Public viewer uses one protected read-only credential file
decisions.text: The cPanel-hosted viewer accepts only /home/learning/.blackcat/github_token, outside the public web root, with private permissions. Missing or unsafe credential state fails closed; no environment, hard-coded or cache fallback is accepted. This credential is repository-read only and must never be reused as a signing trust root.

decisions.title: UEFI QEMU tests use explicit OVMF pflash state
decisions.text: Boot-smoke workflows pair a non-secboot OVMF CODE image with its matching writable VARS template through pflash drives. Firmware-launch failures remain separate from ISO-build evidence.

decisions.title: PR workflows use evidence-aware concurrency
decisions.text: Hosted/read-only jobs cancel superseded PR copies. The self-hosted live-build preserves an active run but collapses older pending duplicates, avoiding unsafe mid-build interruption while prioritizing the newest candidate revision.

decisions.title: Current Test Candidate is separate from Approved ISO
decisions.text: The viewer may expose one exact smoke-passed GitHub Actions artifact for operator physical testing, clearly labelled TEST CANDIDATE — NOT AN APPROVED RELEASE. Approved release distribution remains a separate promotion state.

decisions.title: Systemd is the sole Black Cat quick-check evidence producer
decisions.text: Physical testing showed that executing the collector again from the normal-user profile hook conflicts with root-owned /run/blackcat reports. The systemd service now produces evidence exactly once; the login hook is display-only and static tests enforce that boundary.

decisions.title: Automation Manifesto pre-pause check is mandatory
decisions.text: Safe reversible auditable in-scope work proceeds automatically. Before asking for routine permission or pausing because CI is running, the assistant must apply the Automation Manifesto pre-pause checklist. Human interruption is reserved for physical, destructive/irreversible, authorization, trust-ownership, secret, commitment, material-policy or genuinely unresolved-information gates.

decisions.title: Boot branding is reproducible but cosmetic
decisions.text: Black Cat boot imagery is staged from repository-controlled bytes with a pinned SHA-256 and independent static decode check. GRUB/UEFI and Syslinux/legacy may display the branding, but inability to render it must never alter trust classification or remove ordinary boot choices.

decisions.title: Decode before digest for text-encoded binary assets
decisions.text: A pinned digest is meaningful only after the text transport successfully reconstructs the binary. Boot-image preparation therefore validates source existence, successful base64 decode and then exact decoded SHA-256 before staging any branding bytes.

changelog.summary: Initial trust chain and threat model.
Established GitHub as canonical workspace and expanded documentation.
Locked Prototype 1 baseline and mandatory lessons-learned process.
Added safe first-stage build tooling and static validation.
Paused Community Compute Commons implementation, restored exclusive focus to core Prototype 1, and added the single-command first real-builder evidence collector.
Provisioned the first remote Debian 13 builder and formalized weak-to-strong progressive hardening as a mandatory project rule.
Established the self-hosted GitHub Actions execution path, completed the first real-builder evidence run, and separated the cloud build-host role from later UEFI/TPM attestation testing.
Verified the builder toolchain, fixed the runner PATH false negative and live-build directory mismatch, and advanced to the first ISO build milestone.

Rebranded the user-facing project as Black Cat while retaining PTL internals, recorded the first successful physical USB boot, and added a no-typing System Check boot path for real-hardware diagnostics.
Added a controlled approved-ISO download panel so CI candidates cannot be mistaken for an approved release; the release button remains disabled until an exact ISO is explicitly promoted.

Hardened the public project viewer to fail closed by removing embedded/fallback credentials and stale authoritative release data; approved downloads additionally require a valid source commit plus a passed smoke test.
Synchronized the public viewer with its working single protected token-file deployment and corrected the integrated QEMU UEFI smoke harness to use explicit OVMF CODE/VARS pflash state.

Added evidence-aware per-PR workflow concurrency so superseded hosted/read-only jobs are cancelled while an active self-hosted live-build is allowed to finish and redundant pending builds collapse to the newest revision.

Recorded the successful integrated M13B build/UEFI/QEMU smoke run, froze the exact physical-test ISO identity, and split the living viewer into a Current Test Candidate download path plus an independent Approved Black Cat ISO release gate.

Recorded the first physical no-typing System Check result, fixed duplicate root/user diagnostic execution, added a regression guard, and superseded the buggy candidate pending corrected rebuild and physical retest.

Added the Black Cat Automation Manifesto, made its pre-pause check a mandatory project rule, added static enforcement, surfaced it on the living project page, and formalized proceed-by-default autonomy up to genuine human gates.

Added reproducible Black Cat project-icon boot branding for GRUB/UEFI and Syslinux/legacy, pinned the decoded splash SHA-256, added static asset/menu checks, and kept branding cosmetic so it cannot become a boot or trust dependency.

Recorded the first branding CI failure as malformed base64 transport, removed the ambiguous large asset, replaced it with a compact 160x120 8-colour splash, and added explicit decode-before-digest validation before staging branding into the live image.
